attribute_drawn: The independent review of the 2017 season reported more than 1.2 million ha burned, about 65,000 evacuees, suppression costs above 568 million dollars and a 70-day provincial state of emergency, the first since 2003; more than 160 fires started on July 7, 2017, largely from dry lightning, and the review called the mountain pine beetle central to the 2017 fires and the season a sign of a new normal under climate change.
trigger_attributed: climate change; mountain pine beetle; dry lightning storm of July 7, 2017; long hot dry summer and fuel buildup

attribute_drawn: In the Canadian National Fire Database for western Canada, lightning-caused fires from April to September 1981 to 2018 showed a non-significant overall decrease in number (modified Mann-Kendall with Theil-Sen slope), with clusters up to 270 km in southeastern and south-central British Columbia; hexel trends were significantly negative in central eastern BC and positive in parts of northeastern and central BC, and BC showed no trend in clustering.

Defined the start and end of each year's lightning-caused fire season in Alberta and western and eastern Ontario as the dates a smoothed daily fire risk curve crossed thresholds, with interval estimates and permutation tests for linear trend, and found significant changes in both start and end in Alberta and in the end date in both Ontario regions.

From 1018 days of Pinus pinaster needle litter moisture measured in central Portugal from 2014 to 2023, a correction of FFMC-based moisture raised ISI and FWI under dry conditions but did not improve prediction of fire numbers or burned area over the original indices.

In chamber tests at 26.7 °C with humidity stepped between 90 and 20 per cent, response times of recently dead fine fuels ranged from 0.2 to 37 h and of weathered fuels from 0.5 to 10 h, and adsorption was slower than desorption. Full text not open, abstract only.

Bayazit and Önöz showed by simulation that prewhitening corrects the inflated rejection rate of the Mann-Kendall test on autocorrelated trendless series but costs power when a trend exists, and that prewhitening should be avoided when power is already high, that is with low coefficient of variation, steep trend and long record.

FWI and Seasonal Severity Rating computed from NCEP, ERA-40 and ERA-Interim over the Iberian Peninsula were compared with FWI from seven Spanish weather stations; all reanalyses tended to underestimate station FWI, NCEP most, and ERA-Interim reached summer correlations above 0.5 at inland stations and identified extreme days better.

The sensitivity of burned area to inter-annual fire weather across the world's major biomes was non-linear with a saturation threshold above which burned area was insensitive to increasing fire weather.

Across 11 regions from the European Alps to the Mediterranean basin, models with high AUC for fire occurrence could fail to perform well on burned area measured by CLARE, and multi-variable models tended to outperform single fire index models.

In ERA-40 over 1958-2001 the lower tropospheric warming trend of 0.14 K per decade fell to 0.10 K per decade after correction for observing system changes, and the 1979-2001 water vapour trend of 0.36 mm per decade was judged an artefact of new satellite inputs.

Benjamini and Yekutieli proved that the Benjamini-Hochberg step-up procedure still controls the false discovery rate when test statistics have positive regression dependency on the true nulls, and that dividing the level by the sum of 1/i over the m tests controls it under any dependency.

In 35 plots over 161 ha of dry Douglas-fir forest near Knife Creek in the Alex Fraser Research Forest, central British Columbia, 23 fires between 1619 and 1943 burned at intervals of 10 to 30 years, mostly at low to moderate severity, while current fire-free intervals of 72 to 184 years exceed the historical maximum. The authors attributed the dense modern stands to the twentieth-century shift from Indigenous fire stewardship and settler fires to fire exclusion and suppression, and opened with the 2.55 million ha burned in BC in 2017 and 2018.
trigger_attributed: end of Indigenous fire stewardship and settler burning; fire exclusion and suppression in the twentieth century

attribute_drawn: On the Iberian Peninsula, 1980 to 2017, extreme fire weather days were defined as days with Daily Severity Rating above the 95th percentile in summer, and their monthly distribution was highly correlated with normalised burnt area.

Common fire-weather indices and weather variables were compared as predictors of fire occurrence and size in Mediterranean France within Firelihood, against a baseline model with only spatial and seasonal effects. Indices alone rated fire activity poorly, spatial and seasonal effects were needed, the Canadian FWI was the most skilful index, and combinations of DC, DMC, FFMC with vapour pressure deficit or maximum temperature and wind did better still.

Fourteen crossdated fire-scar records from dry forests of the Montane Cordillera Ecozone showed 32 years of moderate fire synchrony and 4 years of high synchrony between 1746 and 1945; synchronous fire years had below-average precipitation and summer drought, and fire occurrence and synchrony fell after 1945 with fire exclusion, suppression and climatic variation. The authors linked current blocking ridges, longer seasons and drought to the synchronous fires of 2017, 2018 and 2021 in British Columbia. CSIRO bot protection blocked the open-access PDF, so only the abstract was read.
trigger_attributed: summer drought and below-average annual precipitation; fire exclusion and suppression after 1945; climate change expressed as blocking high-pressure ridges, longer fire seasons and more drought

attribute_drawn: Forty years of daily fire weather at five stations in the northern Sierra Nevada showed fairly strong upward trends in high to extreme fire weather, particularly since the mid-1990s.

In the northern Sierra Nevada, fire season days above the 90th and 95th Energy Release Component percentiles became more frequent after 1994, and days below the 80th and 50th percentiles declined from the late 1990s and early 2000s.

Daily lightning efficiency, flashes per lightning-caused fire from the Canadian Lightning Detection Network and the National Fire Database, was described for June to August 2000 to 2020 by ecozone and for British Columbia ecoprovinces with ERA5 FWI moisture codes. In the Montane Cordillera efficiency rose quadratically through summer to a predicted 81 flashes per fire on 9 August, the Southern Interior ecoprovince had the highest predicted efficiency, and DMC and DC correlated with efficiency more than FFMC in most zones.

Landsat mapping of burned area in Canada's forested ecozones from 1985 to 2015 found a significant Theil-Sen increase of 2.4 per cent per year (709.3 ha per year) in the Montane Cordillera, one of only two ecozones with a significant 30-year trend, and the only ecozone with a significant increase in large burned patches over 200 ha; the low Montane Cordillera burn rate was attributed to wet climate, active suppression and rough terrain.
trigger_attributed: no cause attributed to the trend; low burn rate attributed to wet climate, active fire suppression and rough terrain

attribute_drawn: From 157 provincial historical documents and 19 expert interviews, the authors divided the history of fire governance in British Columbia up to 2020 into five eras in which government decision-making superseded First Nations fire governance from the 1870s, in a province that had seen seven catastrophic fire seasons in the twenty-first century. Springer and PubMed Central blocked automated download, so only the abstract was read.
trigger_attributed: government command and control fire governance replacing First Nations fire governance; recent catastrophic fire seasons as a driver of policy change

attribute_drawn: At Ne Sextsine, a 5900 ha dry Douglas-fir forest in T'exelc (Williams Lake First Nation) territory, median fire intervals from 1550 to 1982 were 18 years per plot and 4 years for the site; frequent fire in low-severity plots ended in the 1870s after smallpox, forced relocation and the prohibition of Indigenous burning, and in mixed-severity plots in the 1920s with industrial grazing and logging. Wiley and PubMed Central blocked automated download, so only the abstract was read.
trigger_attributed: end of Indigenous burning after the 1870s (smallpox, relocation, burning prohibition); industrial grazing and logging from the 1920s

attribute_drawn: Three British Columbia case studies illustrated direct and indirect climate effects on forests; for the mountain forests of the East Kootenay region the authors concluded that climate-disturbance interactions are complex and that climate change effects on fire may be amplified by human land use, fire exclusion and mountain pine beetle outbreaks. No open full text was found and CrossRef carried no abstract, so the OpenAlex abstract was used.
trigger_attributed: climate warming; human land use; fire exclusion; mountain pine beetle outbreaks

attribute_drawn: DiCiccio and Efron reviewed the BCa, bootstrap-t, ABC and calibrated bootstrap intervals and showed that the plain percentile interval, the 5th to 95th percentiles of the replications for a 90 per cent interval, is the special case of BCa with no bias or acceleration correction, and that the corrections raise coverage accuracy from first to second order.

Applying several sensitivity methods to the FWI and the McArthur Forest Fire Danger Index on 8 years of gridded Australian data, both indices were most sensitive to wind, then humidity, then temperature, but the FFDI was less sensitive to wind and rain and more to temperature and humidity than the FWI. Full text not open, abstract only.

In the European boreal zone, 1901 to 2017, Monthly Drought Code trended higher in April in the western and in April and May in the northern sections, and large fire years followed July high pressure cells.

Using a simple warming model, HadEX3, 20CR and the De Bilt station record, trends in warm-day counts computed from the same data over the same years differed by about 1 day per decade globally over 1961-2018 (about 25 per cent), 2.4 days in 20CR and 3 days per decade at De Bilt over 1960-2020 (about 50 per cent) when the percentile reference period moved from 1961-1990 to 1981-2010.

Using four hypothetical indices, three of them monotone transformations of one another, the study showed that Mahalanobis distance, percentile analysis and logistic regression statistics ranked effectively identical indices differently, so their differences reflect index frequency distributions; only the c-index treated them as equal, and a ranked-percentile comparator was proposed and applied to the Angström and Nesterov indices at Graz, both with c-index 0.816.

Efron developed bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrap confidence intervals that improve on earlier percentile-type intervals and reach second-order correctness in a wide range of parametric and nonparametric problems.

Built the Global Fire WEather Database of daily FWI System values from 1980 on MERRA reanalysis with alternative gauge precipitation, and compared the Drought Code with station calculations at 48 stations worldwide, finding strong regional biases in both directions traced to reanalysis precipitation.

FWI System components from MERRA-2 for 2004 to 2018 were generally biased low against a global station network, with median biases of -0.2 for FFMC, -6.1 for DMC and -54.7 for DC over each station's four-month fire season, and temperature and humidity biases explained most FWI component bias.

The provincial review of the 2003 season reported over 2,500 wildfire starts from lightning and human causes in the Interior, over 260,000 ha burned, 334 homes destroyed and more than 45,000 people evacuated, following southern BC's driest three-year period on record; it held that decades of successful suppression had built up fuel, citing 70 years of suppression in the Rocky Mountain Trench.
trigger_attributed: three-year drought and hot, dry 2003 summer; lightning and human ignitions; fuel buildup from fire suppression

attribute_drawn: Daily counts of lightning-ignited fires in UTM zone 15 of northwestern Ontario were best estimated from the Duff Moisture Code and the multiplicity of negative lightning discharges, with stepwise linear regression explaining nearly 50 per cent of the variance.

Frei and Schär modelled seasonal counts of rare daily events as binomial with logistic regression trends and found that in a 100-year record a 1.5-fold frequency change was detected with probability 0.6 for events with a 30-day return period but only 0.2 for a 100-day return period, applied to 113 Swiss rain gauges, 1901 to 1994.

A machine-learning attribution of satellite-detected boreal forest fires from 2002 to 2022 separated natural from human causes; human-caused fires declined significantly over the period while natural fires were relatively stable.
Extreme fire weather days in Europe became more frequent, correlated with annual burned area, and rose abruptly at change-points around the late 1990s and mid-2000s in the Mediterranean.

The logarithmic score, the log predictive density at the observation, is strictly proper, is equivalent to the log Bayes factor when comparing forecasting rules, and relates to cross-validation; scores of competing forecasts are only directly comparable over the same set of forecast situations.

Using grid cells across Ontario and a new algorithm that dates each year's season from observed fires, fire season length increased across much of northern Ontario, by a median of about 0.5 days per year in the northwest and 0.25 days per year in the northeast, through earlier human-caused starts and later lightning-caused ends.

Hall and Wilson set two rules for bootstrap tests, that resampling should reflect the null hypothesis, for instance by centring the bootstrap statistic on the observed estimate, and that the test should borrow constructions known to give accurate confidence intervals; breaking the first rule can sharply reduce power.

Across eight boreal fire management regions of Canada from 1979 to 2018, a drier end-of-season DC was followed by more human-caused spring fires in most regions but not by larger burned area or lower suppression success, and overwinter precipitation alone was a poor indicator of spring drought.

In seven forest plots in Alberta and Ontario with soil moisture probes, the daily Drought Code tracked moisture in organic layers at 10 to 18 cm well, better than land surface model estimates, which underpredicted organic layer moisture.

Fire-scar records from eight sites in west central British Columbia gave 46 local and 16 moderate fire years between 1600 and 1900 and 17 regionally synchronous fire years; drought (PDSI) increasingly synchronised fire from local to regional scales, whereas ENSO, PDO and PNA had a weak or inconsistent influence from 1700 to 1900, except that regional fires were significantly associated with years when ENSO and PDO were both positive.
trigger_attributed: interannual drought (PDSI); ENSO and PDO in positive phase together; antecedent moisture driving fine fuel growth at local scale

attribute_drawn: This provincial review expected the southern interior of British Columbia to see the largest projected increases in fire weather indices, reported correlations between seasonal drought and annual area burned from r = 0.20 to r = 0.73 across biogeoclimatic zones (after Meyn et al. 2010), and traced the severity of the mountain pine beetle outbreak that began in the late 1990s partly to fire history, fire suppression and harvesting that shaped lodgepole pine age structure.
trigger_attributed: climate warming and drought; fire suppression, fire history and harvesting shaping pine age structure; mountain pine beetle; lightning

attribute_drawn: On the Iberian Peninsula, FWI computed from ERA-Interim and regional climate model daily mean inputs was biased low against FWI from 12 UTC instantaneous inputs, with the component ratio 0.94 for FFMC and 0.55 for ISI, and daily mean data detected on average 55 per cent of 12 UTC extreme days. Mean seasonal severity could be corrected linearly but threshold exceedance (FWI above 30) could not.

This review of western North American forests, with a section on British Columbia, stated that burned area in BC is mainly controlled by annual to decadal climate and fire weather rather than fuel, that fuel availability governs severity, and that more than 1.2 million ha burned in each of 2017 and 2018; fire scar records show fire nearly eliminated from plateau and mountain forests by the late nineteenth to early twentieth centuries.
trigger_attributed: annual to decadal climate and fire weather; fire exclusion and end of Indigenous cultural burning; insect outbreaks including mountain pine beetle

attribute_drawn: In Douglas-fir and ponderosa pine forests of the southern interior of British Columbia, 41 plots over 1105 ha gave fire scars on 125 trees and establishment dates for 1270 trees; 76 per cent of plots held fire-scarred trees with a mean plot-composite fire scar interval of 21 years over 1700 to 1900, and 66 per cent of plots were of mixed severity through time.

Hirsch, Slack and Smith introduced the seasonal Kendall test and the seasonal Kendall slope estimator, a Theil-Sen type median of pairwise slopes, for skewed, seasonal environmental records, and showed the slope estimator was unbiased with higher precision than regression for skewed data but not an exact test under serial correlation.

Jain, Wang and Flannigan computed the Canadian FWI System from the North American Regional Reanalysis for 1979 to 2015 and tested trends in fire season length, spread days and the 99th percentile of FWI with Theil-Sen slopes, Mann-Kendall tests and field significance, finding mostly positive significant trends.

The late June 2021 Pacific Northwest heat dome, a persistent positive 500 hPa height anomaly, accounted for 21 to 34 per cent of North American area burned in 2021 and was 59 per cent longer and 34 per cent larger than it would have been without warming, estimated by removing the 1979-2020 Theil-Sen trend in geopotential height; British Columbia burned 0.7 Mha (0.48 per cent of land area) in 2021 by MODIS.
weather_input_stated: ERA5 reanalysis, hourly at 0.25 degree; the hour used for the daily FWI is not stated; computed with the cffdrs R package
trigger_attributed: 2021 heat dome (blocking ridge); anthropogenic warming of the lower atmosphere

attribute_drawn: Jolly and co-authors derived fire weather season length from three reanalyses and three fire danger indices for 1979 to 2013 and, using Theil-Sen slopes and Mann-Kendall tests with a four-step correction for serial autocorrelation, found seasons lengthened over 29.6 million square kilometres, 25.3 per cent of the vegetated surface, an 18.7 per cent increase in global mean season length.

In southern Ontario tallgrass prairie, fuel load averaged 0.70 kg m-2 (0.38 to 0.96), a moisture model for fully cured matted grass predicted surface moisture of cured grass in spring, and 25 spring head fires spread at 4 to 55 m min-1. Full text not open, abstract only.

More than 45 million cloud-to-ground flashes recorded by the Canadian Lightning Detection Network over 1999 to 2018 were mapped on 10 km squares; sensor upgrades improved detection efficiency and location accuracy but left large-scale patterns similar to 1999 to 2008.

Künsch extended the jackknife and bootstrap to general stationary sequences by resampling blocks of consecutive observations rather than single values, and gave conditions under which block estimates of standard error were consistent, namely a block length that grows with the sample size but more slowly than it.
Negative binomial regression for count data with extra-Poisson variation was examined for the efficiency and robustness of its inference and compared with quasi-likelihood methods.

Daily lightning- and human-caused fire occurrence in British Columbia, 1981 to 2000, was modelled by year-specific logistic regressions on 950 cells of 20 by 20 km with lightning strikes, weather, stability indices and FWI System moisture codes. Under leave-one-year-out cross-validation the daily provincial count correlated with observations at R = 0.83 for lightning fires and R = 0.55 for human-caused fires, with lower skill for a 75 000 km2 region.

A satellite-based forest fire weather index for the Himalaya, 2000 to 2024, showed significant trends and interannual anomalies with elevated danger in El Nino years and reduced danger in La Nina phases.

A daily people-caused fire occurrence procedure for northern Ontario combined logistic regression for the probability of a fire day with a Poisson assumption for daily counts, and a 1984 summer field test found it worked well in relatively wet periods.

Periodic functions of calendar day were added to logistic models of daily people-caused fire occurrence in northern Ontario to represent seasonal variation, and the models were tested on three independent years.

Compared the Forest Fire Danger Index, the Forest Fire Behaviour Tables and the Canadian FWI across a grid of wind, fuel moisture and fuel availability and on thirteen years of weather station data from Camden airport, New South Wales; the indices shared a structure but rated identical inputs very differently, and differences partly cancelled when each used its own observation time and sub-models.

Computed global FWI System values from ERA5 HRES for 1979 to 2018 with the DC either overwintered or reset to 15 each spring, validated against Environment and Climate Change Canada stations (mean Spearman correlation 0.77), and showed large early-season DC and FWI differences between the two start-up rules, for example in 2016 over North America.

Across 16 landscape regions of British Columbia from 1920 to 2000, annual wildfire extent and occurrence declined, and the decline was significantly related to wetter summers measured by the self-calibrating Palmer Drought Severity Index and an aridity index, with the strength of that relation differing between landscapes. Full text was blocked by the publisher and the HAL copy, so the trend test and the regional slopes were not read.

For the North Okanagan, British Columbia, the Canadian Forest Fire Danger Rating System run under multiple climate scenarios projected a 30 per cent longer fire season and a 95 per cent increase in summer fire weather severity by 2070, with fire behaviour shifting toward intermittent and full crown fire. No open full text was found, so the index version and weather inputs could not be checked.

Önöz and Bayazit compared prewhitening, trend-free prewhitening, variance correction and block bootstrap versions of the Mann-Kendall test by simulation, found block bootstrap power comparable with the others, and gave the block length that minimises Type I error as a function of sample size and autocorrelation, applied to Turkish annual streamflow.

For Greece, 2000 to 2016, the EFFIS FWI danger class thresholds were too low, and four sets of thresholds fitted by cluster analysis and non-linear regression significantly improved the predictability of wildfire danger.

Described the British Columbia provincial fuel type layer, built from Vegetation Resource Inventory polygons (over 4.7 million polygons across more than 94 million ha) assigned to FBP System fuel types by rule, and stated that the typing is inherently subjective because many BC vegetation communities fall between FBP fuel types.

Daily numbers of human-caused bushfires in 10 management areas of south-west Western Australia were modelled by negative binomial regression on fuel moisture, recent fire counts, work day and rainfall, fitted on three years and tested on an independent year; fit was reasonable everywhere but day-to-day variability was useful only in densely populated areas dominated by deliberate ignitions.

Proposed an objective weather-based classification of days into spread events and non-spread events for fire-growth modelling with the FBP System; the abstract does not state the FWI value used, which later papers cite as FWI above 19.

Politis and Romano introduced the stationary bootstrap, which resamples blocks of random, geometrically distributed length so that the resampled series is itself stationary, and proved its consistency and weak convergence for weakly dependent stationary observations.

Review showing that random cross-validation of temporally, spatially or hierarchically structured ecological data seriously underestimates predictive error, and that blocked cross-validation addresses this if blocks are chosen with care about extrapolation.

From the same WRF forecast output over western North America, an hourly FWI built on the Van Wagner (1977) hourly FFMC was compared with the standard daily FWI against observation-based daily FWI at 917 fire weather stations. Noon hourly values were biased low, daily maximum hourly values ran slightly above the daily FWI, and correlations were similar (r 0.71 to 0.75 against 0.75 for the daily method on day 1, per Table 1).

The aggregate FWI carries the caveat that the same value may be produced by different combinations of weather variables; large fire weather typologies on the Iberian Peninsula were heat-driven, heat wave, seasonal drought and wind-driven.

A meta-analysis of peer-reviewed studies from 2000 to 2021 on mountain pine beetle outbreaks and later wildfire in western Canada and the USA found limited consensus; spatial scale, forest fuels and weather explained the spread of results, with red-stage stands and stand-scale fuel and weather studies tied to amplified fire and landscape-scale studies to dampened fire. Springer blocked automated download, so only the abstract was read.
trigger_attributed: mountain pine beetle outbreak stage; forest fuels; weather; spatial scale of analysis

attribute_drawn: Santer and co-authors compared temperature trends from satellite, radiosonde and reanalysis data sets over 1979 to 1993 and 1959 to 1996 and showed that overlapping confidence intervals for separate trends hid differences that a test on the trend of the difference series found, with about 30 per cent of data set pairs differing significantly in lower tropospheric trend, mainly because of the measurement system.
Litter and 10-hour fuel moisture measured in eight forest stands in southern Germany, where fire records are sparse, gave a reasonable ranking of fire danger indices by Spearman rank correlation.

At a National Renewable Energy Laboratory tower in complex terrain in Colorado, 22 years of observations showed no significant trend in the Hot-Dry-Windy Index, whereas ERA5 for the same period and for 67 years showed strong increasing trends across Colorado, and ERA5 underestimated wind speed in a way resolution alone did not explain. Despite its title, the index is the Hot-Dry-Windy Index, not the Canadian FWI. Full text not open, abstract only.

The Forestry Canada Fire Danger Group described the rating system as four modules, the Fire Weather Index System, the then new Fire Behavior Prediction System, a proposed Fire Occurrence Prediction System and an incomplete Accessory Fuel Moisture System meant to carry fuel-specific moisture codes such as cured grass and deciduous litter. The text layer is an OCR scan with character errors, so quotes were taken only from clean passages.

The 2016 Fort McMurray fire weather was very likely an outcome of anthropogenic effects on a persistent upper ridge; ENSO and PDO were not found to contribute to wildfire weather in western Canada, and spring warming and drying since 1871 could not be attributed to common teleconnections.

Reviewed the development and implementation of the rating system in Canada and abroad, describing two primary subsystems (FWI and FBP) with accessory fuel moisture and fire occurrence elements, and argued that research, data infrastructure, training and inter-agency cooperation must develop together.

Review of statistical wildfire prediction centred on North American agency records. It traces daily occurrence models from a negative binomial count model on a danger index (Bruce 1960) and a Poisson model on FFMC (Cunningham and Martell) to logistic GAMs, notes that Poisson count models face overdispersion that logistic models of binary cell-days avoid, and states that lightning detection data miss strikes in a spatially nonrandom way.
Essay arguing that reanalyses to date contained unphysical time-varying biases that limit or defeat their use for long-term trends, and calling for a reanalysis strategy built for homogeneity.

Tiao and co-authors showed, using ozone and rawinsonde temperature records, that the precision of a trend estimate depends critically on autocorrelation in monthly observations and on record length, while being insensitive to the daily sampling rate under systematic sampling.

The temperature and relative humidity functions of 16 fire danger and spread models differed substantially, and three hypothetical climate change scenarios gave projections from minimal change to more than a 50 per cent increase, with non-trivial differences between models designed for similar fuels.

Across the Czech Republic at 500 m, 1956 to 2015, most of the territory showed an increasing frequency of fire weather days, with trends accelerating after 2000; fuel aridity explained more than two thirds of reported wildfire variability in 1991 to 2015.

FWI System indices computed from raw and homogenised weather at 16 Canadian stations differed by Wilcoxon signed-rank test at most stations; homogenising the 66-year records reduced index values by about 0.7 to 8.4 per cent and reversed the long-term trend at some stations, such as Kapuskasing.

Venäläinen and co-authors computed the FWI from ERA-40 and ERA-Interim for Europe, 1960 to 2012, with Sen slopes and a Mann-Kendall test corrected for autocorrelation through effective sample size, and found no clear trend over 1960 to 1999 but a mean FWI increase significant at the 99 per cent level in southern and eastern Europe over 1980 to 2012.

A blind benchmark of 25 homogenization contributions on simulated monthly temperature and precipitation networks with inserted breaks found that performance depended on the error metric and that only the best algorithms improved precipitation; the paper cites network-wide changes, including observation time and the move to automatic stations, that biased regional trends, such as half a degree in the Greater Alpine Region.

Comparing the SPI, self-calibrated PDSI and the new SPEI on station records from several climates, with synthetic warming of 2 and 4 C added over 1910-2007, only the two indices that include evapotranspiration registered more severe drought under warming; the authors held that the choice of PET method was not critical.

Described the ERA5-based fire danger reanalysis, whose inputs are assembled from hourly forecast strips to approximate local noon everywhere, and compared it with the ERA-Interim version and the Global Fire Weather Database, finding regional mean biases of -5 to +5 and anomaly correlations of 0.52 to 0.87, with larger differences in mountainous areas.

Over 1979-2008 the adjusted US Historical Climatology Network warmed 0.327 C per decade, close to the mean of six reanalyses (0.342, range 0.280 to 0.437), while the raw network warmed less than every reanalysis; a shift from afternoon to morning observation at about 20 per cent of stations had imposed an artificial 0.20 C cooling.

Wang and co-authors showed by Monte Carlo simulation that Mann-Kendall power rises with slope, sample length and significance level and falls with noise variance, and that positive autocorrelation raises both Type I and Type II error by enlarging the variance of the test statistic.

From daily observations at 25 stations in six Alpine countries, 1951 to 2010, the FWI and other indices increased significantly in the Western and Southern Alps with more days above a predefined threshold, weakly in the Northern Alps and not clearly in inner Alpine valleys; in Bavaria meteorological fire danger rose while fire numbers and area burned fell.
Comparing weather types with FFMC, DMC and DC at five Alpine stations, regional differences were largest for FFMC, then DMC, then DC, attributed to the time lags of the fuel layers.

Weatherhead and co-authors derived formulae for the number of years needed to detect a linear trend given noise variance and lag-one autocorrelation, finding roughly 10 to more than 20 years for a 5 per cent per decade trend, and showed that a level shift such as an instrument change can raise the required record length by 50 per cent or more.

In western US federal forest fire records, the fire season measured from first discovery to last control of large fires averaged more than 84 days longer in 2003-2012 than in 1973-1982, about three days per year, and the earliest third of snowmelt years held more than 70 per cent of large forest fire area over 1970-2012.

Lightning and lightning-caused fires in southern British Columbia and Alberta differed across the Continental Divide, with one fire per 50 lightning discharges in British Columbia against one per 1400 in Alberta; elevation, strike distribution, Daily Severity Rating and vegetation controlled lightning fire occurrence.

Wilks built moving blocks bootstrap tests for differences of means in serially correlated climate data and showed that applying the same resampled time blocks to every element of a data vector carries the cross correlation between elements into the resampled statistics without modelling it, with accurate test levels in small samples.

Wilks found that 97 of 281 Journal of Climate papers from the first half of 2014 (34.5 per cent) mapped nominally significant local tests while only 3 (1.1 per cent) addressed multiple testing, and showed by simulation that the false discovery rate procedure stays robust under spatial correlation, becoming conservative so that setting the FDR level at twice the global level restores approximately correct test levels.

Lightning fire occurrence in Ontario was split into the probability that a strike gives a sustained ignition and the probability that the ignition is detected, fitted by ecoregion from strike, weather and fire records. A sheltered duff moisture index was the strongest ignition predictor everywhere, positive cloud-to-ground strikes raised ignition probability except in the far northwest, and post-storm weather mattered.

Using Canadian Forest Service litter moisture samples collected at sites across Canada from 1939 to 1961, forest type, season, stand density and duff moisture each changed the relation between FFMC and measured litter moisture, and a model adjusting FFMC for these factors was fitted. Full text not open, abstract only.

Monthly fire counts in the January to April season, 1996 to 2007, across counties of Qiannan prefecture, Guizhou, China, were fitted with Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated and hurdle models with and without county random effects; the negative binomial mixed model performed best in the model comparisons, ahead of zero-inflated and hurdle negative binomial forms.

Yue, Pilon, Phinney and Cavadias showed by Monte Carlo simulation that serial correlation changes the variance of the Mann-Kendall statistic, that a trend biases the estimated lag-one autocorrelation, and that prewhitening removes part of a real trend, so they proposed removing the trend before estimating autocorrelation, applied to streamflow in Ontario, Canada.

Zhang and co-authors showed by Monte Carlo simulation that counts of days above a percentile threshold estimated from a 30-year base period are biased low inside and high outside that period, producing a spurious jump and trend in trendless data that grows with the percentile and with autocorrelation, and removed it with a bootstrap in-base estimate.

Review of the internationally coordinated extremes indices, reporting that indices built on fixed physical thresholds have limited relevance across climates and that the field moved toward relative, percentile-defined thresholds, and documenting the practical obstacles to computing and gridding them.

In Scots pine, larch and oak stands of the south-eastern Great Xing'an Mountains, China, in summer and autumn 2014, the standard hourly FFMC underestimated measured dead fine fuel moisture, while a locally calibrated hourly FFMC fitted well (R2 0.920 to 0.969, RMSE 4.09 to 7.87). Full text not open, abstract only.

From burned area at mid to high northern latitudes, 1982 to 2018, temperature-driven flammability increased wildfire in fuel-rich forests while rising flammability with fuel reduced by water deficits decreased it, and human ignition had polarised effects.
